correctness.rationale: Exact Bernstein derivative coefficients have one strictly positive entry, leading via Descartes rule and endpoint signs to the complete all-degree classification. Telescoping jump decomposition is an exact BV seminorm norm reduction, and the Poisson limit of both response and derivative plus unique finite-degree maximum establishes the sharp first-step boundary constant.

originality.rationale: Searches for the Boolean-sum formula, step-response critical points, bounded-variation operator norms and boundary Poisson layers found no theorem whose implications include the exact structural classification and the first-jump limit. Materially inspected prior texts focus on approximation rates. Earlier 1984 and 1994 papers remained inaccessible for complete priority checks and are explicitly named as residual risks.

value.rationale: The two-extremum rigidity and exact sharp step reduction classify instability of the standard twofold Boolean acceleration for every degree. A nonvanishing, explicitly located Poisson-scale overshoot is structurally relevant to the mismatch between smooth convergence acceleration and discontinuous-data BV stability; this is not a routine low-degree numerical artifact.
